We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthesis steps reverse: target -> break amide to give acid + aniline (or amine). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid decarboxylates to give acid). So we need to identify the unsaturated acid fragment: /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is part of the side chain attached to sulfonyl phenyl. The target has /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid is a cinnamic acid derivative (trans). So retrosynthesis: target -> remove amide to give cinnamic acid (with sulfonyl phenyl attached) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break cinnamic acid to give aromatic aldehyde (p-? Actually the aromatic ring attached to sulfonyl is c2ccc(... )cc2). The aldehyde would be the same aromatic ring with aldehyde at para position? The side chain is attached to that ring via the double bond. So the aldehyde is p-formyl phenyl attached to sulfonyl? The unsaturated acid is formed from aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl) + malonic acid via Doebner, giving p-(cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl phenyl. So reverse: cinnamic acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (or malonic acid decarboxylates). So step 2: break C=C and C=O to give aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then step 3: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride?) Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to tolyl ring (para methyl). So sulfonamide formed from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl) and an aniline (the other phenyl with amine). So reverse: break sulfonamide to give p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and aniline (the phenyl with amine). But the aniline is part of the target: the NS(=O)(=O) attached to tolyl ring, and the N is attached to the other phenyl (c3ccccc3N). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group and also to the other phenyl? Wait SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: tolyl ring (Cc1ccc(... )cc1) attached to N (the sulfonamide nitrogen). That N is attached to S(=O)(=O) which is attached to another phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (as an aniline) and to the sulfonyl group. The sulfonyl group attaches to second phenyl ring which has the side chain. So sulfonamide formation: aniline (tolyl amine) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) to give sulfonamide. So reverse: break sulfonamide to give tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl with sulfonyl chloride). However the second phenyl also has side chain; after breaking, we have aryl sulfonyl chloride attached to side chain? Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) with a Cl instead of the side chain? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring via S=O2Cl attached to that ring. In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to that ring and also to the N. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same phenyl ring with a sulfonyl chloride substituent (Ar-SO2Cl). The side chain is attached to that phenyl ring via the carbon (the aromatic carbon bearing the side chain). So the sulfonyl chloride would have both the side chain and the sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring at a position (maybe para). The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O). So the sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl ring at the position where the side chain is attached? Wait the SMILES: S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring at the same carbon as the side chain? No, the sulfonyl group attaches to the phenyl carbon (the aromatic carbon) and the side chain is attached to the same phenyl ring at a different position (para maybe). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride attached (Ar-SO2Cl) and the side chain still present (the unsaturated acid). So step 3 reverse: break N-S bond to give p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (Cl-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(... )cc2). Good.

Thus we need to construct route JSON with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We have some templates from earlier search: template 733 is sulfonamide formation (Cl-SO2-aryl + aniline -> sulfonamide). That matches our sulfonamide step. So we can use template_id 733.

For amide formation: need a template that forms amide from carboxylic acid and amine. Search maybe for amide formation template. Let's search for functional_groups_formed "amide".
